artefacts.description: Full wizard round-trip: all six selections persist in POST /restore/jobs 201 response
GET /restore/jobs/:id returns job with all wizard selections intact
assertions: GET returns same jobId as POST response

artefacts.description: Skip is the default conflict mode when conflictMode is omitted from POST /restore/jobs
assertions: conflictMode=skip when not supplied in request body
This mirrors the RestoreWizard UI where Skip is pre-selected as the default

artefacts.description: GET /restore/jobs/:id confirms skip default persists in store
assertions: GET returns conflictMode=skip after omitting conflictMode on POST

artefacts.description: All three conflict modes (override, skip, ask) round-trip correctly through POST and GET
assertions: POST with conflictMode=override → 201 + GET returns override
POST with conflictMode=skip → 201 + GET returns skip
POST with conflictMode=ask → 201 + GET returns ask

artefacts.description: Destination=original with scope=all (no trash check) → 201 job created
assertions: scope=all skips the trash-window check (no Jira API call)

artefacts.description: Destination=alternate → targetProjectKey present in response (drives UI project picker)
assertions: destination.targetProjectKey=OPS persists (drives the Alternate project picker in UI)

artefacts.description: Destination=export → 201 created, no targetProjectKey, RestoreWorker (skeleton) calls no Jira write API
assertions: no targetProjectKey present on export destination
RestoreWorker skeleton does not call any Jira write API (Sprint 12 delivers writes)

artefacts.description: Alternate destination without targetProjectKey → 400 INVALID_DESTINATION
POST /restore/jobs with trashed project + original destination → 409 TRASH_WINDOW_BLOCK with alternate-location guidance
Original destination stays blocked for trashed project — both repeated POSTs return 409
Alternate destination succeeds even when project is in trash window — user can restore to a different location
assertions: POST with destination=alternate → 201 (no trash check for alternate)
User can proceed with restore after switching from Original to Alternate

artefacts.description: Export destination succeeds for trashed project — no Jira in-place write, no trash check
assertions: POST with destination=export → 201 regardless of project trash status

artefacts.description: Ask-mode job seeds to awaiting_decision — UI surfaces conflict decision prompt
assertions: After seeding awaiting_decision + conflict, GET returns status=awaiting_decision

artefacts.description: POST /decisions with override transitions job from awaiting_decision → running
POST /decisions with skip also transitions job from awaiting_decision → running
POST /decisions when job is not awaiting_decision → 409 INVALID_STATE
assertions: message contains "Current status:" (references the current non-awaiting status)

artefacts.description: RestoreWorker checkStall() marks job stalled when heartbeat gap >20s; stalled event emitted on bus and [jira-restore] log line captured
assertions: [jira-restore] job.stalled log line emitted with correct jobId and lastHeartbeatAgeMs

artefacts.description: After stall, next heartbeat clears stalled flag and emits [jira-restore] job.recovered log
Stalled flag set in RestoreJobStore (via setStalled) is readable via test endpoint; SSE stream publishes stalled events via RestoreEventBus
assertions: test endpoint exposes raw stalled field for signal verification
SSE stream delivers stalled events published by RestoreWorker.checkStall()
